summary:
Daejeon has no separate legal regime of its own; the national law of South Korea governs transgender residents and visitors in the city. What is documented here runs through a court seated in Daejeon and through a cemetery. On 7 October 2021 the Daejeon District Court ordered the cancellation of the Army's discharge of Staff Sergeant Byun Hee-soo, the first known legal case involving a transgender soldier. The court held that the military should have treated her as female following her legal sex change, that the loss of genitalia was not a valid ground for dismissal, and that a fitness-for-service review must weigh basic rights. The decision upheld the appeal pursued on her behalf after her death.

On 24 June 2024 Byun Hee-soo was buried at the National Cemetery in Daejeon; she was Korea's first transgender soldier. Around 60 activists protested at the burial, arguing that it was marred by discriminatory treatment. The ceremony was conducted as an official state honour in the city.
tangentialFactors:
The two Daejeon findings are both attached to one person's case and to institutions seated in the city rather than to any local law. The Daejeon District Court's holding that the loss of genitalia is not valid grounds for dismissal was directed at the basis the military had used to end her service, so the ruling's reach is defined by the national framework it applied rather than by anything municipal.

The official state honour conferred at the Daejeon burial coincided with an activist protest over discriminatory treatment in how it was carried out, and the classification the military had applied to her post-surgical status was the basis the Daejeon court rejected.
localsOnly:
For residents of Daejeon, the city's district court is the forum where the discharge of a transgender soldier was reversed, and the National Cemetery in Daejeon is where she is buried. Around 60 activists attended the June 2024 burial to protest discriminatory treatment in its handling.

The court's reasoning on fitness review and on the irrelevance of genitalia loss is recorded at district court level in Daejeon; no separate city policy on transgender matters appears in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the Daejeon District Court's holdings have been applied in later military fitness or discharge cases is not sourced. No Daejeon-specific statute, municipal ordinance, police practice, school restroom policy, healthcare rule or hate-crime enforcement record appears in the inventory.

The Daejeon inventory rests on two news reports, one from Yonhap dated 7 October 2021 and one from Aju Press dated 25 June 2024; no court document or official transcript is cited.
